notes: Hard debugging task: a 25-commit git repository (17 files, pure stdlib) whose hot path was accidentally made O(n^2) by one commit in the middle of history. dependent_stages=3: the benchmark run bases every later stage (bisect classification -> fault localization -> algorithmic fix -> benchmark regression test -> bench.json evidence); the suite must stay green and the new test must fail against a re-introduced regression or the whole task fails. reasoning_depth=3: the agent must reason about complexity scaling, separate the harness/tests/other modules from the offending hot path, and choose a fix plus a timing test design that is robust on a loaded single CPU. debugging_ambiguity=3: the regression is invisible to the correctness suite (everything passes), it must be located across a commit range with git bisect driven by wall-clock classification, and the exact file/commit is not named anywhere in the instruction. hidden_case_generalization=2: verifier times the hot path at 3 hidden sizes (20k/40k/80k) against a reference implementation and re-introduces the regression in a scratch repo. quantitative_correctness=3: runtime must stay within a generous factor of the reference at every hidden size and the agent's own benchmark test must fail on the regressed copy while passing on the fixed one. resource_pressure=1: leaving the regression in place makes the verifier's runs take tens of seconds, which is the only pressure. No irreversible actions, no live services.
